The crossbar R_AR state must either: (a) buffer/register the address+valid from R_IDLE and hold s_arvalid=1 in R_AR regardless of current m_arvalid, OR (b) present s_arvalid combinatorially from m_arvalid in R_IDLE (before the registered R_AR state), giving arready to the master in the same cycle the address is decoded. Option (b) avoids a register and costs 0 cycles. Option (a) requires an address/valid latch in the read engine.

fix_requests.summary: GH #93 regression: SoC does not boot at all on feat/cpu-domain-cdc-gh93 (commit 66a9af1) -- CPU never commits a single instruction (0/8 PCs, 0/100 boot-stability attempts).
fix_requests.expected_behavior: Per docs/design/RTL_DEFINITION.md / fr_null_20260603_052800_00 (already-fixed CPU RESET_PC bug): after rst_n_i/cpu_rst_n_i release and PLL lock, the CPU must synchronously load RESET_PC=0x0000_1000 and begin committing instructions from boot ROM within a few hundred cycles.
fix_requests.observed_behavior: Verified via `make soc_boot` (tb/cocotb/soc/, commit 66a9af1, pristine working tree): test_boot_pc_scoreboard FAILS with 'timeout: collected 0/8 commits'; test_boot_sram_sentinels FAILS identically (golden reference model confirms SRAM[0x2000]=0xDEADBEEF/[0x2004]=0x12345678 are correct pre-flight, but the DUT never gets far enough to write them); test_boot_stability_100 FAILS on every single observed attempt (22+ consecutive attempts with varied reset-phase offsets and random seeds, all 'timeout: collected 0/8 commits', 0/100 before the run was stopped as conclusive). Root cause (confirmed by independent RTL trace, cross-checked against a second agent's identical finding): rtl/soc/soc_top.sv's u_cpu_clk_en_sync (cdc_2ff_sync gating cpu_gated_clk via u_cpu_cg, rooted at cpu_core_rst_n) and u_cpu_pmu_rst_sync (feeds cpu_domain_rst_n = cpu_core_rst_n & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync, also rooted at cpu_core_rst_n) are both 2-stage synchronizers with an already-asserted (=1) source value (pmu_cpu_clk_en and pmu_cpu_rst_n both default to 1 out of pmu.sv reset), so both transition 0->1 on the SAME cpu_core_clk edge (2 cycles after cpu_core_rst_n releases). rv32i_clock_gate's ICG (rtl/mem/rv32i_clock_gate.sv) only updates its enable latch while clk is low, so cpu_gated_clk's first toggle coincides with cpu_domain_rst_n's release -- there is no cpu_gated_clk edge while cpu_domain_rst_n is still asserted. u_cpu's pipeline (rtl/cpu/core/pipeline/rv32i_pipeline_if.sv and siblings) uses plain synchronous reset (`always_ff @(posedge clk) if (!rst_n) pc_q <= RESET_PC`), which requires at least one clock edge WHILE rst_n is low to actually load the reset value -- since that never happens, pc_q keeps its uninitialized/0 simulation value instead of RESET_PC=0x1000, and the CPU fetches from an unmapped address forever. Blast radius: every SoC-level cocotb suite that boots real CPU firmware through tb_soc_top/tb_soc_pll is blocked -- soc_boot, soc_periph, soc_coherency, soc_cpu_gpu, soc_pll (commit_pc-dependent checks), plus the newly-authored soc_multiclock and soc_pll_multiclock suites. This is a regression against the prior 142/142 soc_all baseline (pre-commit 66a9af1).

This keeps cpu_gated_clk = cpu_core_clk running unconditionally for the entire cpu_core_rst_n-low window (the safe cdc_2ff_sync reset value now matches the required safe state), so u_cpu (and u_cpu_axi_cdc's s-side cdc_reset_sync, same s_clk_i=cpu_gated_clk) both see clock edges throughout cpu_domain_rst_n's assertion and correctly load their synchronous reset values, including RESET_PC. Added extensive header comments documenting the reset-release ordering with cycle counts, plus sanity-check findings for pmu_cpu_iso_en_sync's safe reset value, u_cpu_pmu_rst_sync's rst_n_i choice, and async_axi_fifo's reset-hold contract. Per AXI4 protocol, a slave must not assert xREADY in a way that causes a master to complete a legal handshake (valid&&ready) whose transaction is then silently discarded -- if the bridge cannot yet accept a transfer (because its own reset has not fully released), wr_ready_o/s_arready_o must read 0, not 1.
fix_requests.observed_behavior: Root-caused via a throwaway (uncommitted, reverted) 1ns free-running Timer() diagnostic probe added to test_soc_multiclock.py, driving the SoC at the CPU_PERIOD_NS=3/FABRIC_PERIOD_NS=7 ratio and sampling cpu_domain_rst_n, core_rst_n, cpu_axi_arvalid_raw, cpu_bridge_s_arvalid/s_arready, and xbar_m_arvalid/arready[0] every 1ns from t=0: t=0ns cpu_domain_rst_n=0 core_rst_n=0 (both in reset); t=33ns cpu_domain_rst_n=1 core_rst_n=0 (CPU-domain reset releases FIRST -- its PLL locks in 16*3ns=48ns vs the fabric PLL's 16*7ns=112ns, an asymmetry impossible at the pre-GH#93 1:1 ratio where both PLLs shared one clock net); t=45ns cpu_axi_arvalid_raw=1 s_arvalid=1 s_arready=1 (the CPU's first I$-miss AR handshake completes -- s_arready_o reads 'ready' even though core_rst_n, and therefore rst_both_n=s_rst_n_i&m_rst_n_i, and therefore the FIFO's own wr_rst_n_i=s_rst_sync_n, are all STILL 0/in-reset); t=48ns cpu_axi_arvalid_raw=0 (the CPU, per AXI4 protocol, never re-asserts arvalid for an already-completed handshake -- the transaction is gone); t=98ns core_rst_n=1 (fabric reset finally releases, 40ns too late). Confirmed pc_q (rtl/cpu/core/pipeline/rv32i_pipeline_if.sv) loads RESET_PC=0x1000 correctly (proving fix fr_57f49b7f9b29 works) but never advances past it -- ic_valid_o=1/ic_stall_i=1 persist (a permanent, unrecovered I-cache miss) because the dropped AR request's response never arrives. make soc_multiclock: TESTS=4 PASS=0 FAIL=4 (all four tests fail identically -- 0 commits or PASS_PC never reached). make soc_pll_multiclock: TESTS=1 PASS=0 FAIL=1 (last committed PC=0x00000000, same class of stall -- CPU never boots far enough to even reach the APB_PLL2 MMIO path this suite targets, so it provides no independent evidence about apb_cdc_bridge specifically). Code-level root cause: rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_gray_fifo.sv line ~166 `full_q <= 1'b0` on `!wr_rst_n_i` (async reset default = not full), and line ~173 `assign wr_ready_o = !full_q;` (no gating on wr_rst_n_i itself). wr_rst_n_i is s_rst_sync_n (async_axi_fifo.sv), derived from rst_both_n = s_rst_n_i & m_rst_n_i. While m_rst_n_i (core_rst_n) is still low, s_rst_sync_n is also still low, so the FIFO's own `always_ff @(posedge wr_clk_i or negedge wr_rst_n_i) if (!wr_rst_n_i) ... else if (push) ...` can only take the reset branch every cycle -- no push logic ever executes -- yet wr_ready_o already reads 1 purely because full_q's reset value happens to be 0. apb_cdc_bridge.sv (GH #93's other new CDC primitive) is NOT expected to share this exact defect: its s_pready_o = (s_state_q == S_DONE), and s_state_q resets to S_IDLE (!= S_DONE) via the same rst_both_n-derived s_rst_sync_n, so its ready output correctly defaults to 0 (not ready) while held in reset -- consistent with its own 15/15 passing unit suite, which explicitly covers independent-side mid-transaction reset. This cannot be confirmed empirically at the SoC level because soc_pll_multiclock's firmware needs the CPU to boot first, which this same bug prevents.

rtl_response.diff_summary: cdc_gray_fifo.sv: wr_ready_o changed from `!full_q` to `wr_rst_n_i && !full_q` (lines ~172-186). full_q's async reset value is 1'b0 ('not full'), so on its own !full_q read 1 for the entire window the write domain was held in reset, while wr_bin_q was simultaneously held at 0 by the same reset -- a write master could complete a handshake whose beat was then silently dropped, never committed to mem_q/wr_bin_q. Gating wr_ready_o directly on wr_rst_n_i (a same-domain input, not a cross-domain signal -- no new CDC path introduced) makes the FIFO correctly backpressure (ready=0) for the entire reset window, matching rd_valid_o's existing correct behaviour (empty_q already resets to 1'b1). Also updated two header comments in cdc_gray_fifo.sv (the no-combinational-crossing note and the full_q/empty_q derivation site) to describe the new gating precisely. async_axi_fifo.sv was read but NOT edited -- its header claim 'while a domain is held in reset, both its ready and valid outputs are 0' was FALSE before this fix and is TRUE after it, so no comment correction was needed there. apb_cdc_bridge.sv audited, confirmed already safe by construction (s_pready_o = (s_state_q==S_DONE), s_state_q resets to S_IDLE != S_DONE) -- not touched. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: re-running the GH #91 unit suite (tb/cocotb/soc, make async_axi_fifo) after this fix gives 21/22, not 22/22. The one new failure, test_reset_while_busy_s_side, was root-caused (via a throwaway, uncommitted, reverted scratch diagnostic outside tb/ -- see design_state history reason) to a testbench-timing assumption that only held under the OLD buggy RTL: previously, s_wready read 1 throughout the entire reset pulse (the bug), so the test's still-running interrupted AXI master task completed its whole burst falsely and instantly *inside* the reset window itself, long before the test's post-release wait + t.kill()/_idle_s_side() calls -- so it never had a chance to touch the post-reset FIFO. With the fix, the master genuinely blocks (ready=0) through reset, so it is still mid-burst when reset releases; empirically confirmed (scratch probe) that s_wready recovers ~2 s_clk cycles after release while the interrupted task's s_wvalid is still 1, so it legitimately completes 2+ more real W beats into the FRESH FIFO before the test's kill() call several cycles later -- an AXI-protocol-compliant master resuming a genuinely-blocked burst, not an RTL defect. This is a testbench race exposed (not caused) by correcting the RTL, and cannot be resolved without editing tb/ (out of scope per this task's constraints -- verification-orchestrator owns tb/ and should adjust the test's kill/idle timing, e.g. kill the interrupted task before or at reset assertion rather than after release).
